{"content":"name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
description: >-
  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
  future leak.)

inputs:
  repo-url:
    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
    required: false
    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
  preserve-path:
    description: >-
      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
    required: false
    default: ''
  preserve-cache-dir:
    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
    required: false
    default: ''

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
        cd /tmp
        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

        # Park the preserved path (per-arch build cache) outside the
        # workspace first — the clean below removes everything else.
        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ]; then
          SRC="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$PRESERVE"
          if [ -d "$SRC" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing $PRESERVE in $CACHE..."
            rm -rf "$CACHE"
            mkdir -p "$CACHE"
            mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"
          fi
        fi

        # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
        # shared workspace (bench leftovers held by docker containers) —
        # log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
        if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
        fi
        if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
          if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
          fi
        fi
        mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

        CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a live
          # bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build the
          # checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A bench
          # leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path; if one
          # ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_TARGET"
        if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
          while IFS= read -r entry; do
            name="$(basename "$entry")"
            if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
              echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
            else
              mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
            fi
          done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ] && [ -d "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" ]; then
          echo "Restoring $PRESERVE from $CACHE..."
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")"
          mv "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")/"
        fi

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: same pin on `build-macos` (audit); its checkout rides the new action.
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new composite action, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script functionally smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, and clone-around branches all produce a valid checkout.
- Related guard suites (workflow fetch shape, dispatch watch, selfhosted SDK): 79 tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `runs-on: fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the registration label that routes to it is `macos-m5` (the existing pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005) — pinned that way.
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class and out of scope; AC3 (next daily green) needs that leg resolved too.
- bench-mls.yml also runs `self-hosted` but only orchestrates remote sandboxes (no local containers → nothing unremovable); plain leftovers are handled by the tolerant clean.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `daily-publish` testflight leg fails — `Submit iOS to TestFlight → Install fastlane` dies with `bundle: command not found` (exit 127), and on the 2026-10-15 night run the `Build iOS IPA` job additionally failed at the custom mirror-checkout with `rm: cannot remove … jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/…`.

**Root cause**: Two independent layers in the shared self-hosted fleet:

1. **Routing (F-A)** — `Build iOS IPA` and `Submit iOS to TestFlight` in `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` (jobs `build-ios`, `submit-ios`) pin the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`. The fleet has a Linux self-hosted box whose advertised labels also satisfy that list, so the iOS jobs route onto Linux — no ruby/bundler/fastlane/Xcode there, hence `bundle: command not found` (exit 127 at *Install fastlane*) and `security: command not found` later. The repo already has the correct unique pin for its ONE self-hosted macOS M5 runner (`fa-m5-1`, registered with the custom label `macos-m5`): `ci.yml`'s `cube-kernel-live` uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` (gh-1005). The same vulnerable generic shape sits on `build-macos.yml`'s `build-macos` job (the daily CLI leg builder).

2. **Workspace isolation (F-B)** — `bench-harbor.yml`'s `bench` job (dispatchable onto the self-hosted box via `cpu-runner`) runs harbor with `-o jobs`, writing its job output INTO `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` (`jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/` = `fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${kind}-${shard}`). On a persistent self-hosted runner the workspace is SHARED across workflow runs, and harbor's docker sandbox leaves trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers; the leftovers (sqlite files under active mounts) cannot be removed. The mobile legs' custom mirror-checkout then runs a bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` → `rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1 → the checkout fails before any build step. `build-macos.yml` carries the same bare `rm -rf` pattern (sites: build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos).

**Impact**: Every scheduled `daily-publish` testflight leg fails (and would keep failing) — no TestFlight build ships. The failure is independent of the code being built; L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget, #1262) blocks the CLI leg separately and is out of scope here.

**Fix approach**:
- **F-A**: pin `build-ios`, `submit-ios` (build-mobile.yml) and `build-macos` (build-macos.yml) to `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the label only `fa-m5-1` carries (the ticket's `fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; `macos-m5` is the registration label that routes to it, per gh-1005/ci.yml). REG: workflow-lint test asserts every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS publish legs carries `macos-m5` and never the generic `macOS`/`ARM64` labels.
- **F-B**: (a) bench-harbor writes its job output OUTSIDE the build workspace — `-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace path); artifact upload + Harbor Hub upload follow the same path. (b) an `if: always()` cleanup step in the bench job tears the shard's docker containers down (`docker rm -f` name-filtered by the pinned `--job-name`) BEFORE removing the output dir. (c) the three mirror-checkouts are hardened into a shared composite action (`.github/actions/mirror-checkout`, same pattern as `setup-flutter-selfhosted`) whose clean step is log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and as a last resort clone into a sibling dir and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can no longer fail the checkout.
- **Audit**: no other macOS-only leg uses the generic shape — `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live already pins `macos-m5`; nightly/build-macos-cli matrix runners are hosted (`macos-latest`/`macos-15-intel`). bench-mls.yml also runs `runs-on: self-hosted` but only orchestrates REMOTE sandboxes (Daytona/Modal — no local containers, nothing unremovable), and its plain leftovers are removed by the tolerant clean.

{"content":"name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
description: >-
  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
  future leak.)

inputs:
  repo-url:
    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
    required: false
    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
  preserve-path:
    description: >-
      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
    required: false
    default: ''
  preserve-cache-dir:
    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
    required: false
    default: ''

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
        cd /tmp
        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

        # Park the preserved path (per-arch build cache) outside the
        # workspace first — the clean below removes everything else.
        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ]; then
          SRC="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$PRESERVE"
          if [ -d "$SRC" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing $PRESERVE in $CACHE..."
            rm -rf "$CACHE"
            mkdir -p "$CACHE"
            mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"
          fi
        fi

        # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
        # shared workspace (bench leftovers held by docker containers) —
        # log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
        if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
        fi
        if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
          if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
          fi
        fi
        mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

        CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a live
          # bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build the
          # checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A bench
          # leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path; if one
          # ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_TARGET"
        if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
          while IFS= read -r entry; do
            name="$(basename "$entry")"
            if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
              echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
            else
              mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
            fi
          done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ] && [ -d "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" ]; then
          echo "Restoring $PRESERVE from $CACHE..."
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")"
          mv "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")/"
        fi

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: same pin on `build-macos` (audit); its checkout rides the new action.
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new composite action, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script functionally smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, and clone-around branches all produce a valid checkout.
- Related guard suites (workflow fetch shape, dispatch watch, selfhosted SDK): 79 tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `runs-on: fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the registration label that routes to it is `macos-m5` (the existing pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005) — pinned that way.
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class and out of scope; AC3 (next daily green) needs that leg resolved too.
- bench-mls.yml also runs `self-hosted` but only orchestrates remote sandboxes (no local containers → nothing unremovable); plain leftovers are handled by the tolerant clean.

**Bug**: The `daily-publish` testflight leg fails — `Submit iOS to TestFlight → Install fastlane` dies with `bundle: command not found` (exit 127), and on the 2026-10-15 night run the `Build iOS IPA` job additionally failed at the custom mirror-checkout with `rm: cannot remove … jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/…`.

**Root cause**: Two independent layers in the shared self-hosted fleet:

1. **Routing (F-A)** — `Build iOS IPA` and `Submit iOS to TestFlight` in `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` (jobs `build-ios`, `submit-ios`) pin the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`. The fleet has a Linux self-hosted box whose advertised labels also satisfy that list, so the iOS jobs route onto Linux — no ruby/bundler/fastlane/Xcode there, hence `bundle: command not found` (exit 127 at *Install fastlane*) and `security: command not found` later. The repo already has the correct unique pin for its ONE self-hosted macOS M5 runner (`fa-m5-1`, registered with the custom label `macos-m5`): `ci.yml`'s `cube-kernel-live` uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` (gh-1005). The same vulnerable generic shape sits on `build-macos.yml`'s `build-macos` job (the daily CLI leg builder).

2. **Workspace isolation (F-B)** — `bench-harbor.yml`'s `bench` job (dispatchable onto the self-hosted box via `cpu-runner`) runs harbor with `-o jobs`, writing its job output INTO `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` (`jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/` = `fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${kind}-${shard}`). On a persistent self-hosted runner the workspace is SHARED across workflow runs, and harbor's docker sandbox leaves trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers; the leftovers (sqlite files under active mounts) cannot be removed. The mobile legs' custom mirror-checkout then runs a bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` → `rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1 → the checkout fails before any build step. `build-macos.yml` carries the same bare `rm -rf` pattern (sites: build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos).

**Impact**: Every scheduled `daily-publish` testflight leg fails (and would keep failing) — no TestFlight build ships. The failure is independent of the code being built; L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget, #1262) blocks the CLI leg separately and is out of scope here.

**Fix approach**:
- **F-A**: pin `build-ios`, `submit-ios` (build-mobile.yml) and `build-macos` (build-macos.yml) to `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the label only `fa-m5-1` carries (the ticket's `fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; `macos-m5` is the registration label that routes to it, per gh-1005/ci.yml). REG: workflow-lint test asserts every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS publish legs carries `macos-m5` and never the generic `macOS`/`ARM64` labels.
- **F-B**: (a) bench-harbor writes its job output OUTSIDE the build workspace — `-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace path); artifact upload + Harbor Hub upload follow the same path. (b) an `if: always()` cleanup step in the bench job tears the shard's docker containers down (`docker rm -f` name-filtered by the pinned `--job-name`) BEFORE removing the output dir. (c) the three mirror-checkouts are hardened into a shared composite action (`.github/actions/mirror-checkout`, same pattern as `setup-flutter-selfhosted`) whose clean step is log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and as a last resort clone into a sibling dir and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can no longer fail the checkout.
- **Audit**: no other macOS-only leg uses the generic shape — `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live already pins `macos-m5`; nightly/build-macos-cli matrix runners are hosted (`macos-latest`/`macos-15-intel`). bench-mls.yml also runs `runs-on: self-hosted` but only orchestrates REMOTE sandboxes (Daytona/Modal — no local containers, nothing unremovable), and its plain leftovers are removed by the tolerant clean.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-1600.

{"content":"name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
description: >-
  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
  future leak.)

inputs:
  repo-url:
    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
    required: false
    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
  preserve-path:
    description: >-
      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
    required: false
    default: ''
  preserve-cache-dir:
    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
    required: false
    default: ''

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
        cd /tmp
        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

        # Park the preserved path (per-arch build cache) outside the
        # workspace first — the clean below removes everything else.
        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ]; then
          SRC="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$PRESERVE"
          if [ -d "$SRC" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing $PRESERVE in $CACHE..."
            rm -rf "$CACHE"
            mkdir -p "$CACHE"
            mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"
          fi
        fi

        # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
        # shared workspace (bench leftovers held by docker containers) —
        # log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
        if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
        fi
        if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
          if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
          fi
        fi
        mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

        CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a live
          # bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build the
          # checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A bench
          # leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path; if one
          # ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_TARGET"
        if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
          while IFS= read -r entry; do
            name="$(basename "$entry")"
            if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
              echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
            else
              mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
            fi
          done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ] && [ -d "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" ]; then
          echo "Restoring $PRESERVE from $CACHE..."
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")"
          mv "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")/"
        fi
","path":".github/actions/mirror-checkout/action.yml"}

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: same pin on `build-macos` (audit); its checkout rides the new action.
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new composite action, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script functionally smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, and clone-around branches all produce a valid checkout.
- Related guard suites (workflow fetch shape, dispatch watch, selfhosted SDK): 79 tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `runs-on: fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the registration label that routes to it is `macos-m5` (the existing pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005) — pinned that way.
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class and out of scope; AC3 (next daily green) needs that leg resolved too.
- bench-mls.yml also runs `self-hosted` but only orchestrates remote sandboxes (no local containers → nothing unremovable); plain leftovers are handled by the tolerant clean.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `daily-publish` testflight leg fails — `Submit iOS to TestFlight → Install fastlane` dies with `bundle: command not found` (exit 127), and on the 2026-10-15 night run the `Build iOS IPA` job additionally failed at the custom mirror-checkout with `rm: cannot remove … jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/…`.

**Root cause**: Two independent layers in the shared self-hosted fleet:

1. **Routing (F-A)** — `Build iOS IPA` and `Submit iOS to TestFlight` in `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` (jobs `build-ios`, `submit-ios`) pin the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`. The fleet has a Linux self-hosted box whose advertised labels also satisfy that list, so the iOS jobs route onto Linux — no ruby/bundler/fastlane/Xcode there, hence `bundle: command not found` (exit 127 at *Install fastlane*) and `security: command not found` later. The repo already has the correct unique pin for its ONE self-hosted macOS M5 runner (`fa-m5-1`, registered with the custom label `macos-m5`): `ci.yml`'s `cube-kernel-live` uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` (gh-1005). The same vulnerable generic shape sits on `build-macos.yml`'s `build-macos` job (the daily CLI leg builder).

2. **Workspace isolation (F-B)** — `bench-harbor.yml`'s `bench` job (dispatchable onto the self-hosted box via `cpu-runner`) runs harbor with `-o jobs`, writing its job output INTO `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` (`jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/` = `fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${kind}-${shard}`). On a persistent self-hosted runner the workspace is SHARED across workflow runs, and harbor's docker sandbox leaves trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers; the leftovers (sqlite files under active mounts) cannot be removed. The mobile legs' custom mirror-checkout then runs a bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` → `rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1 → the checkout fails before any build step. `build-macos.yml` carries the same bare `rm -rf` pattern (sites: build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos).

**Impact**: Every scheduled `daily-publish` testflight leg fails (and would keep failing) — no TestFlight build ships. The failure is independent of the code being built; L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget, #1262) blocks the CLI leg separately and is out of scope here.

**Fix approach**:
- **F-A**: pin `build-ios`, `submit-ios` (build-mobile.yml) and `build-macos` (build-macos.yml) to `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the label only `fa-m5-1` carries (the ticket's `fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; `macos-m5` is the registration label that routes to it, per gh-1005/ci.yml). REG: workflow-lint test asserts every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS publish legs carries `macos-m5` and never the generic `macOS`/`ARM64` labels.
- **F-B**: (a) bench-harbor writes its job output OUTSIDE the build workspace — `-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace path); artifact upload + Harbor Hub upload follow the same path. (b) an `if: always()` cleanup step in the bench job tears the shard's docker containers down (`docker rm -f` name-filtered by the pinned `--job-name`) BEFORE removing the output dir. (c) the three mirror-checkouts are hardened into a shared composite action (`.github/actions/mirror-checkout`, same pattern as `setup-flutter-selfhosted`) whose clean step is log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and as a last resort clone into a sibling dir and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can no longer fail the checkout.
- **Audit**: no other macOS-only leg uses the generic shape — `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live already pins `macos-m5`; nightly/build-macos-cli matrix runners are hosted (`macos-latest`/`macos-15-intel`). bench-mls.yml also runs `runs-on: self-hosted` but only orchestrates REMOTE sandboxes (Daytona/Modal — no local containers, nothing unremovable), and its plain leftovers are removed by the tolerant clean.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-1600.

{"content":"name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
description: >-
  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
  future leak.)

inputs:
  repo-url:
    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
    required: false
    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
  preserve-path:
    description: >-
      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
    required: false
    default: ''
  preserve-cache-dir:
    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
    required: false
    default: ''

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
        cd /tmp
        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

        # Park the preserved path (per-arch build cache) outside the
        # workspace first — the clean below removes everything else.
        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ]; then
          SRC="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$PRESERVE"
          if [ -d "$SRC" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing $PRESERVE in $CACHE..."
            rm -rf "$CACHE"
            mkdir -p "$CACHE"
            mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"
          fi
        fi

        # gh-1600 AC2: tolerate stale unremovable paths in the persistent
        # shared workspace (bench leftovers held by docker containers) —
        # log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
        if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
        fi
        if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
          if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
          fi
        fi
        mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

        CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a live
          # bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build the
          # checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A bench
          # leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path; if one
          # ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_TARGET"
        if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
          while IFS= read -r entry; do
            name="$(basename "$entry")"
            if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
              echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
            else
              mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
            fi
          done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ] && [ -d "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" ]; then
          echo "Restoring $PRESERVE from $CACHE..."
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")"
          mv "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")/"
        fi

{"newText":"      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout — the bare `rm -rf
      # "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` used to fail the whole checkout on stale
      # unremovable leftovers in the persistent shared workspace (bench
      # docker leftovers, jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/). The per-arch build
      # cache below is parked outside the workspace before the clean and
      # restored after the clone (preserve-path/preserve-cache-dir).
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        uses: ./.github/actions/mirror-checkout
        with:
          preserve-path: build/macos
          preserve-cache-dir: '$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-${{ matrix.arch }}'","oldText":"      # ── Checkout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirrors
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          MIRROR_BASE="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror"
          MAIN_MIRROR="$MIRROR_BASE/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          ARCH="${{ matrix.arch }}"
          BUILD_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/build-cache/macos-$ARCH"

          echo "HOME=$HOME"
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MAIN_MIRROR=$MAIN_MIRROR"
          echo "ARCH=$ARCH"

          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            rm -rf "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mkdir -p "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR"
            mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/build/macos" "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/"
          fi

          cd /tmp
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          echo "Cloning main repo with mirror reference..."
          git clone --reference "$MAIN_MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          if [ -d "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" ]; then
            echo "Restoring macOS build cache for $ARCH..."
            mkdir -p build
            mv "$BUILD_CACHE_DIR/macos" build/
          fi","path":".github/workflows/build-macos.yml"}

      - name: Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: same pin on `build-macos` (audit); its checkout rides the new action.
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new composite action, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `daily-publish` testflight leg fails — `Submit iOS to TestFlight → Install fastlane` dies with `bundle: command not found` (exit 127), and on the 2026-10-15 night run the `Build iOS IPA` job additionally failed at the custom mirror-checkout with `rm: cannot remove … jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/…`.

**Root cause**: Two independent layers in the shared self-hosted fleet:

1. **Routing (F-A)** — `Build iOS IPA` and `Submit iOS to TestFlight` in `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` (jobs `build-ios`, `submit-ios`) pin the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`. The fleet has a Linux self-hosted box whose advertised labels also satisfy that list, so the iOS jobs route onto Linux — no ruby/bundler/fastlane/Xcode there, hence `bundle: command not found` (exit 127 at *Install fastlane*) and `security: command not found` later. The repo already has the correct unique pin for its ONE self-hosted macOS M5 runner (`fa-m5-1`, registered with the custom label `macos-m5`): `ci.yml`'s `cube-kernel-live` uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` (gh-1005). The same vulnerable generic shape sits on `build-macos.yml`'s `build-macos` job (the daily CLI leg builder).

2. **Workspace isolation (F-B)** — `bench-harbor.yml`'s `bench` job (dispatchable onto the self-hosted box via `cpu-runner`) runs harbor with `-o jobs`, writing its job output INTO `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` (`jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/` = `fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${kind}-${shard}`). On a persistent self-hosted runner the workspace is SHARED across workflow runs, and harbor's docker sandbox leaves trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers; the leftovers (sqlite files under active mounts) cannot be removed. The mobile legs' custom mirror-checkout then runs a bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` → `rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1 → the checkout fails before any build step. `build-macos.yml` carries the same bare `rm -rf` pattern (sites: build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos).

**Impact**: Every scheduled `daily-publish` testflight leg fails (and would keep failing) — no TestFlight build ships. The failure is independent of the code being built; L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget, #1262) blocks the CLI leg separately and is out of scope here.

**Fix approach**:
- **F-A**: pin `build-ios`, `submit-ios` (build-mobile.yml) and `build-macos` (build-macos.yml) to `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the label only `fa-m5-1` carries (the ticket's `fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; `macos-m5` is the registration label that routes to it, per gh-1005/ci.yml). REG: workflow-lint test asserts every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS publish legs carries `macos-m5` and never the generic `macOS`/`ARM64` labels.
- **F-B**: (a) bench-harbor writes its job output OUTSIDE the build workspace — `-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace path); artifact upload + Harbor Hub upload follow the same path. (b) an `if: always()` cleanup step in the bench job tears the shard's docker containers down (`docker rm -f` name-filtered by the pinned `--job-name`) BEFORE removing the output dir. (c) the three mirror-checkouts are hardened into a shared composite action (`.github/actions/mirror-checkout`, same pattern as `setup-flutter-selfhosted`) whose clean step is log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and as a last resort clone into a sibling dir and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can no longer fail the checkout.
- **Audit**: no other macOS-only leg uses the generic shape — `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live already pins `macos-m5`; nightly/build-macos-cli matrix runners are hosted (`macos-latest`/`macos-15-intel`). bench-mls.yml also runs `runs-on: self-hosted` but only orchestrates REMOTE sandboxes (Daytona/Modal — no local containers, nothing unremovable), and its plain leftovers are removed by the tolerant clean.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-1600.

{"content":"name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
description: >-
  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
  future leak.)

inputs:
  repo-url:
    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
    required: false
    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
  preserve-path:
    description: >-
      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
    required: false
    default: ''
  preserve-cache-dir:
    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
    required: false
    default: ''

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
        cd /tmp
        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: same pin on `build-macos` (audit); its checkout rides the new action.
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new composite action, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script functionally smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, and clone-around branches all produce a valid checkout.
- Related guard suites (workflow fetch shape, dispatch watch, selfhosted SDK): 79 tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `runs-on: fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the registration label that routes to it is `macos-m5` (the existing pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005) — pinned that way.
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class and out of scope; AC3 (next daily green) needs that leg resolved too.
- bench-mls.yml also runs `self-hosted` but only orchestrates remote sandboxes (no local containers → nothing unremovable); plain leftovers are handled by the tolerant clean.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `daily-publish` testflight leg fails — `Submit iOS to TestFlight → Install fastlane` dies with `bundle: command not found` (exit 127), and on the 2026-10-15 night run the `Build iOS IPA` job additionally failed at the custom mirror-checkout with `rm: cannot remove … jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/…`.

**Root cause**: Two independent layers in the shared self-hosted fleet:

1. **Routing (F-A)** — `Build iOS IPA` and `Submit iOS to TestFlight` in `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` (jobs `build-ios`, `submit-ios`) pin the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`. The fleet has a Linux self-hosted box whose advertised labels also satisfy that list, so the iOS jobs route onto Linux — no ruby/bundler/fastlane/Xcode there, hence `bundle: command not found` (exit 127 at *Install fastlane*) and `security: command not found` later. The repo already has the correct unique pin for its ONE self-hosted macOS M5 runner (`fa-m5-1`, registered with the custom label `macos-m5`): `ci.yml`'s `cube-kernel-live` uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` (gh-1005). The same vulnerable generic shape sits on `build-macos.yml`'s `build-macos` job (the daily CLI leg builder).

2. **Workspace isolation (F-B)** — `bench-harbor.yml`'s `bench` job (dispatchable onto the self-hosted box via `cpu-runner`) runs harbor with `-o jobs`, writing its job output INTO `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` (`jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/` = `fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${kind}-${shard}`). On a persistent self-hosted runner the workspace is SHARED across workflow runs, and harbor's docker sandbox leaves trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers; the leftovers (sqlite files under active mounts) cannot be removed. The mobile legs' custom mirror-checkout then runs a bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` → `rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1 → the checkout fails before any build step. `build-macos.yml` carries the same bare `rm -rf` pattern (sites: build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos).

**Impact**: Every scheduled `daily-publish` testflight leg fails (and would keep failing) — no TestFlight build ships. The failure is independent of the code being built; L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget, #1262) blocks the CLI leg separately and is out of scope here.

**Fix approach**:
- **F-A**: pin `build-ios`, `submit-ios` (build-mobile.yml) and `build-macos` (build-macos.yml) to `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the label only `fa-m5-1` carries (the ticket's `fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; `macos-m5` is the registration label that routes to it, per gh-1005/ci.yml). REG: workflow-lint test asserts every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS publish legs carries `macos-m5` and never the generic `macOS`/`ARM64` labels.
- **F-B**: (a) bench-harbor writes its job output OUTSIDE the build workspace — `-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace path); artifact upload + Harbor Hub upload follow the same path. (b) an `if: always()` cleanup step in the bench job tears the shard's docker containers down (`docker rm -f` name-filtered by the pinned `--job-name`) BEFORE removing the output dir. (c) the three mirror-checkouts are hardened into a shared composite action (`.github/actions/mirror-checkout`, same pattern as `setup-flutter-selfhosted`) whose clean step is log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and as a last resort clone into a sibling dir and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can no longer fail the checkout.
- **Audit**: no other macOS-only leg uses the generic shape — `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live already pins `macos-m5`; nightly/build-macos-cli matrix runners are hosted (`macos-latest`/`macos-15-intel`). bench-mls.yml also runs `runs-on: self-hosted` but only orchestrates REMOTE sandboxes (Daytona/Modal — no local containers, nothing unremovable), and its plain leftovers are removed by the tolerant clean.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-1600.

{"content":"name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
description: >-
  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
  future leak.)

inputs:
  repo-url:
    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
    required: false
    default: 'https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git'
  preserve-path:
    description: >-
      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache
    required: false
    default: ''
  preserve-cache-dir:
    description: 'Directory the preserved path is parked in (required when preserve-path is set; $HOME expands at run time)'
    required: false
    default: ''

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
        cd /tmp
        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: same pin on `build-macos` (audit); its checkout rides the new action.
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new composite action, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script functionally smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, and clone-around branches all produce a valid checkout.
- Related guard suites (workflow fetch shape, dispatch watch, selfhosted SDK): 79 tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `runs-on: fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the registration label that routes to it is `macos-m5` (the existing pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005) — pinned that way.
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class and out of scope; AC3 (next daily green) needs that leg resolved too.
- bench-mls.yml also runs `self-hosted` but only orchestrates remote sandboxes (no local containers → nothing unremovable); plain leftovers are handled by the tolerant clean.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `daily-publish` testflight leg fails — `Submit iOS to TestFlight → Install fastlane` dies with `bundle: command not found` (exit 127), and on the 2026-10-15 night run the `Build iOS IPA` job additionally failed at the custom mirror-checkout with `rm: cannot remove … jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/…`.

**Root cause**: Two independent layers in the shared self-hosted fleet:

1. **Routing (F-A)** — `Build iOS IPA` and `Submit iOS to TestFlight` in `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` (jobs `build-ios`, `submit-ios`) pin the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`. The fleet has a Linux self-hosted box whose advertised labels also satisfy that list, so the iOS jobs route onto Linux — no ruby/bundler/fastlane/Xcode there, hence `bundle: command not found` (exit 127 at *Install fastlane*) and `security: command not found` later. The repo already has the correct unique pin for its ONE self-hosted macOS M5 runner (`fa-m5-1`, registered with the custom label `macos-m5`): `ci.yml`'s `cube-kernel-live` uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` (gh-1005). The same vulnerable generic shape sits on `build-macos.yml`'s `build-macos` job (the daily CLI leg builder).

2. **Workspace isolation (F-B)** — `bench-harbor.yml`'s `bench` job (dispatchable onto the self-hosted box via `cpu-runner`) runs harbor with `-o jobs`, writing its job output INTO `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` (`jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/` = `fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${kind}-${shard}`). On a persistent self-hosted runner the workspace is SHARED across workflow runs, and harbor's docker sandbox leaves trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers; the leftovers (sqlite files under active mounts) cannot be removed. The mobile legs' custom mirror-checkout then runs a bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` → `rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1 → the checkout fails before any build step. `build-macos.yml` carries the same bare `rm -rf` pattern (sites: build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos).

**Impact**: Every scheduled `daily-publish` testflight leg fails (and would keep failing) — no TestFlight build ships. The failure is independent of the code being built; L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget, #1262) blocks the CLI leg separately and is out of scope here.

**Fix approach**:
- **F-A**: pin `build-ios`, `submit-ios` (build-mobile.yml) and `build-macos` (build-macos.yml) to `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the label only `fa-m5-1` carries (the ticket's `fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; `macos-m5` is the registration label that routes to it, per gh-1005/ci.yml). REG: workflow-lint test asserts every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS publish legs carries `macos-m5` and never the generic `macOS`/`ARM64` labels.
- **F-B**: (a) bench-harbor writes its job output OUTSIDE the build workspace — `-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace path); artifact upload + Harbor Hub upload follow the same path. (b) an `if: always()` cleanup step in the bench job tears the shard's docker containers down (`docker rm -f` name-filtered by the pinned `--job-name`) BEFORE removing the output dir. (c) the three mirror-checkouts are hardened into a shared composite action (`.github/actions/mirror-checkout`, same pattern as `setup-flutter-selfhosted`) whose clean step is log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and as a last resort clone into a sibling dir and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can no longer fail the checkout.
- **Audit**: no other macOS-only leg uses the generic shape — `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live already pins `macos-m5`; nightly/build-macos-cli matrix runners are hosted (`macos-latest`/`macos-15-intel`). bench-mls.yml also runs `runs-on: self-hosted` but only orchestrates REMOTE sandboxes (Daytona/Modal — no local containers, nothing unremovable), and its plain leftovers are removed by the tolerant clean.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-1600.

{"content":"name: 'Mirror checkout (self-hosted)'
description: >-
  The shared self-hosted mirror-checkout for the macOS publish legs
  (build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos):
  clone the repo into $GITHUB_WORKSPACE from the persistent local git
  mirror. gh-1600 AC2: the workspace on a persistent self-hosted runner is
  SHARED across workflow runs — bench-harbor used to park jobs/<run-id>/
  (trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers) in it, and the old bare
  `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` exited 1 on the unremovable leftovers,
  failing the checkout before any build step. The clean is now
  log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder
  into $RUNNER_TEMP, and as a last resort clone into a sibling directory
  and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can
  no longer fail the checkout. (The root cause moved the bench output
  outside the workspace: bench-harbor.yml now writes
  $RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs; this tolerance covers stale leftovers and any
  future leak.)

inputs:
  repo-url:
    description: 'Repository URL cloned from the local mirror'
    required: false

  preserve-path:
    description: >-
      Workspace-relative path preserved across the clean (parked in
      preserve-cache-dir before the clean, restored after the clone) —
      e.g. build-macos''s per-arch build cache

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Clean workspace (gh-1600 log-and-prune) and clone from the local mirror
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        REPO_URL='${{ inputs.repo-url }}'
        MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/$(basename "$REPO_URL")"
        PRESERVE='${{ inputs.preserve-path }}'
        CACHE='${{ inputs.preserve-cache-dir }}'
        cd /tmp
        echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

        # Park the preserved path (per-arch build cache) outside the
        # workspace first — the clean below removes everything else.
        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ]; then
          SRC="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$PRESERVE"
          if [ -d "$SRC" ]; then
            echo "Preserving existing $PRESERVE in $CACHE..."
            rm -rf "$CACHE"
            mkdir -p "$CACHE"
            mv "$SRC" "$CACHE/"
          fi

        # shared workspace (bench leftovers held by docker containers) —
        # log-and-prune, never fail the checkout.
        if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
        fi
        if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
          echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
          if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
          fi
        fi
        mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

        CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
          # A mount-point stub survived the prune AND the move-aside (a live
          # bind mount). git clone refuses a non-empty target — build the
          # checkout in a sibling and move it in around the stub. A bench
          # leftover path (e.g. jobs/<run-id>/) is not a repo path; if one
          # ever collides, the move below skips it with a note.
          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 "$REPO_URL" "$CLONE_TARGET"
        if [ "$CLONE_TARGET" != "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
          while IFS= read -r entry; do
            name="$(basename "$entry")"
            if [ -e "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$name" ]; then
              echo "::warning::stub collision on '$name' — left in $CLONE_TARGET (gh-1600)"
            else
              mv "$entry" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/"
            fi
          done < <(find "$CLONE_TARGET" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
          rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
        fi
        echo "Checked out: $(git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" log -1 --oneline)"

        if [ -n "$PRESERVE" ] && [ -d "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" ]; then
          echo "Restoring $PRESERVE from $CACHE..."
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")"
          mv "$CACHE/$(basename "$PRESERVE")" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$(dirname "$PRESERVE")/"
        fi

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: same pin on `build-macos` (audit); its checkout rides the new action.
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new composite action, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script functionally smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, and clone-around branches all produce a valid checkout.
- Related guard suites (workflow fetch shape, dispatch watch, selfhosted SDK): 79 tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `runs-on: fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the registration label that routes to it is `macos-m5` (the existing pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005) — pinned that way.
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class and out of scope; AC3 (next daily green) needs that leg resolved too.
- bench-mls.yml also runs `self-hosted` but only orchestrates remote sandboxes (no local containers → nothing unremovable); plain leftovers are handled by the tolerant clean.

{"content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `daily-publish` testflight leg fails — `Submit iOS to TestFlight → Install fastlane` dies with `bundle: command not found` (exit 127), and on the 2026-10-15 night run the `Build iOS IPA` job additionally failed at the custom mirror-checkout with `rm: cannot remove … jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/…`.

**Root cause**: Two independent layers in the shared self-hosted fleet:

1. **Routing (F-A)** — `Build iOS IPA` and `Submit iOS to TestFlight` in `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml` (jobs `build-ios`, `submit-ios`) pin the GENERIC label list `runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`. The fleet has a Linux self-hosted box whose advertised labels also satisfy that list, so the iOS jobs route onto Linux — no ruby/bundler/fastlane/Xcode there, hence `bundle: command not found` (exit 127 at *Install fastlane*) and `security: command not found` later. The repo already has the correct unique pin for its ONE self-hosted macOS M5 runner (`fa-m5-1`, registered with the custom label `macos-m5`): `ci.yml`'s `cube-kernel-live` uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` (gh-1005). The same vulnerable generic shape sits on `build-macos.yml`'s `build-macos` job (the daily CLI leg builder).

2. **Workspace isolation (F-B)** — `bench-harbor.yml`'s `bench` job (dispatchable onto the self-hosted box via `cpu-runner`) runs harbor with `-o jobs`, writing its job output INTO `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` (`jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/` = `fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${kind}-${shard}`). On a persistent self-hosted runner the workspace is SHARED across workflow runs, and harbor's docker sandbox leaves trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers; the leftovers (sqlite files under active mounts) cannot be removed. The mobile legs' custom mirror-checkout then runs a bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` → `rm: cannot remove …` → exit 1 → the checkout fails before any build step. `build-macos.yml` carries the same bare `rm -rf` pattern (sites: build-mobile.yml build-ios/submit-ios, build-macos.yml build-macos).

**Impact**: Every scheduled `daily-publish` testflight leg fails (and would keep failing) — no TestFlight build ships. The failure is independent of the code being built; L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget, #1262) blocks the CLI leg separately and is out of scope here.

**Fix approach**:
- **F-A**: pin `build-ios`, `submit-ios` (build-mobile.yml) and `build-macos` (build-macos.yml) to `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the label only `fa-m5-1` carries (the ticket's `fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; `macos-m5` is the registration label that routes to it, per gh-1005/ci.yml). REG: workflow-lint test asserts every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS publish legs carries `macos-m5` and never the generic `macOS`/`ARM64` labels.
- **F-B**: (a) bench-harbor writes its job output OUTSIDE the build workspace — `-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"` (runner-managed scratch, never a workspace path); artifact upload + Harbor Hub upload follow the same path. (b) an `if: always()` cleanup step in the bench job tears the shard's docker containers down (`docker rm -f` name-filtered by the pinned `--job-name`) BEFORE removing the output dir. (c) the three mirror-checkouts are hardened into a shared composite action (`.github/actions/mirror-checkout`, same pattern as `setup-flutter-selfhosted`) whose clean step is log-and-prune: remove what is removable, move a still-blocked remainder into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and as a last resort clone into a sibling dir and move the checkout in around the stub — a stale unremovable path can no longer fail the checkout.
- **Audit**: no other macOS-only leg uses the generic shape — `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live already pins `macos-m5`; nightly/build-macos-cli matrix runners are hosted (`macos-latest`/`macos-15-intel`). bench-mls.yml also runs `runs-on: self-hosted` but only orchestrates REMOTE sandboxes (Daytona/Modal — no local containers, nothing unremovable), and its plain leftovers are removed by the tolerant clean.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-1600.
