# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe; the kimi coding plan tolerates more — owner picks at dispatch)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # gh-1503: byte-consistent copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 resolve step
      # (same run block, same outputs) — the single-source extraction was
      # rejected there to keep the workflow self-contained; the
      # cross-reference comment in both files is the sync contract. Maps
      # the provider choice to the full provider triple (type/baseUrl/
      # model/key env) and preflights the selected secret BEFORE the
      # bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
      # must cost one setup minute, not shard-hours of 429s. Presence
      # only: the value …

### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux; same pin on `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (audit).
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, clone-around — all produce a valid checkout. Related guard suites: 79 Dart tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the routing label is `macos-m5` (the pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005).
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class, out of scope; AC3 needs that leg resolved too. `bench/mls_bench` has one PRE-EXISTING python REG failure on pristine main (stale `@4.0.0` dataset pin, #1316 drift) — unrelated to this change.

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: same pin on `build-macos` (audit); its checkout rides the new action.
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new composite action, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script functionally smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, and clone-around branches all produce a valid checkout.
- Related guard suites (workflow fetch shape, dispatch watch, selfhosted SDK): 79 tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `runs-on: fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the registration label that routes to it is `macos-m5` (the existing pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005) — pinned that way.
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class and out of scope; AC3 (next daily green) needs that leg resolved too.
- bench-mls.yml also runs `self-hosted` but only orchestrates remote sandboxes (no local containers → nothing unremovable); plain leftovers are handled by the tolerant clean.

        run_block = self.text.split("Run harbor (fa agent", 1)[1]

    def test_agent_timeout_input_clips_the_watch_ceiling(self):
        # gh-1556 rework review: under the watch the abs ceiling is the
        # cap that actually kills a progressing trial, so an explicit
        # agent-timeout input must clip it to base x4 (pre-PR the legacy
        # ladder did exactly this) — otherwise the tighter cap the
        # operator asked for is silently ignored in favor of the flat
        # 3600s step-env default.
        self.assertIn(
            "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4",
            self._shard_run_block(),
        )

    def test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed(self):
        # gh-1556 rework re-review (suggestion): the escape hatch is
        # "remove the watch exports to restore the legacy ladder" — but
        # the exports are load-bearing individually: unsetting ONLY
        # FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC (keeping agent-timeout set)
        # must not die on an unbound variable under `set -euo pipefail`;
        # the ceiling defaults to base x4 (exactly what the legacy
        # ladder would have used) before the clip runs.
        run_block = self._shard_run_block()
        self.assertIn(

# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe; the kimi coding plan tolerates more — owner picks at dispatch)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}

      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # gh-1503: byte-consistent copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 resolve step

      # bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY

### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux; same pin on `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (audit).
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, clone-around — all produce a valid checkout. Related guard suites: 79 Dart tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the routing label is `macos-m5` (the pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005).
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class, out of scope; AC3 needs that leg resolved too. `bench/mls_bench` has one PRE-EXISTING python REG failure on pristine main (stale `@4.0.0` dataset pin, #1316 drift) — unrelated to this change.

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: same pin on `build-macos` (audit); its checkout rides the new action.
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new composite action, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script functionally smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, and clone-around branches all produce a valid checkout.
- Related guard suites (workflow fetch shape, dispatch watch, selfhosted SDK): 79 tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `runs-on: fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the registration label that routes to it is `macos-m5` (the existing pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005) — pinned that way.
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class and out of scope; AC3 (next daily green) needs that leg resolved too.
- bench-mls.yml also runs `self-hosted` but only orchestrates remote sandboxes (no local containers → nothing unremovable); plain leftovers are handled by the tolerant clean.

        run_block = self.text.split("Run harbor (fa agent", 1)[1]

    def test_agent_timeout_input_clips_the_watch_ceiling(self):
        # gh-1556 rework review: under the watch the abs ceiling is the
        # cap that actually kills a progressing trial, so an explicit
        # agent-timeout input must clip it to base x4 (pre-PR the legacy
        # ladder did exactly this) — otherwise the tighter cap the
        # operator asked for is silently ignored in favor of the flat
        # 3600s step-env default.
        self.assertIn(
            "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4",
            self._shard_run_block(),
        )

    def test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed(self):
        # gh-1556 rework re-review (suggestion): the escape hatch is
        # "remove the watch exports to restore the legacy ladder" — but
        # the exports are load-bearing individually: unsetting ONLY
        # FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC (keeping agent-timeout set)
        # must not die on an unbound variable under `set -euo pipefail`;
        # the ceiling defaults to base x4 (exactly what the legacy
        # ladder would have used) before the clip runs.
        run_block = self._shard_run_block()
        self.assertIn(

# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe; the kimi coding plan tolerates more — owner picks at dispatch)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # gh-1503: byte-consistent copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 resolve step
      # (same run block, same outputs) — the single-source extraction was
      # rejected there to keep the workflow self-contained; the
      # cross-reference comment in both files is the sync contract. Maps

      # bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY

### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux; same pin on `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (audit).
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, clone-around — all produce a valid checkout. Related guard suites: 79 Dart tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the routing label is `macos-m5` (the pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005).
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class, out of scope; AC3 needs that leg resolved too. `bench/mls_bench` has one PRE-EXISTING python REG failure on pristine main (stale `@4.0.0` dataset pin, #1316 drift) — unrelated to this change.

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: same pin on `build-macos` (audit); its checkout rides the new action.
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new composite action, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script functionally smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, and clone-around branches all produce a valid checkout.
- Related guard suites (workflow fetch shape, dispatch watch, selfhosted SDK): 79 tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `runs-on: fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the registration label that routes to it is `macos-m5` (the existing pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005) — pinned that way.
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class and out of scope; AC3 (next daily green) needs that leg resolved too.
- bench-mls.yml also runs `self-hosted` but only orchestrates remote sandboxes (no local containers → nothing unremovable); plain leftovers are handled by the tolerant clean.

self.assertTrue(knobs.progress_extension)

    def test_stall_gap_never_drops_below_the_watchdog_invariant(self):
        # gh-1430 invariant: the bench stall-gap must stay above fa's
        # stream-idle watchdog (300s) + margin — the workflow value can
        # never drift below the shipped default (the Dart-source REG in
        # test_fa_agent_timeout.py pins the other side).
        sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
        try:
            import fa_agent_timeout
        finally:
            sys.path.remove(str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
        gap = float(self._step_env("FA_STALL_GAP_SEC"))
        self.assertGreaterEqual(gap, fa_agent_timeout._STALL_GAP_DEFAULT)

    def _shard_run_block(self):
        """The harbor shard step's `run: |` body."""
        run_block = self.text.split("Run harbor (fa agent", 1)[1]
        return run_block.split("run: |", 1)[1].split("Upload harbor job", 1)[0]

    def test_agent_timeout_input_clips_the_watch_ceiling(self):
        # gh-1556 rework review: under the watch the abs ceiling is the
        # cap that actually kills a progressing trial, so an explicit
        # agent-timeout input must clip it to base x4 (pre-PR the legacy
        # ladder did exactly this) — otherwise the tighter cap the
        # operator asked for is silently ignored in favor of the flat
        # 3600s step-env default.
        self.assertIn(
            "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4",
            self._shard_run_block(),
        )

    def test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed(self):
        # gh-1556 rework re-review (suggestion): the escape hatch is
        # "remove the watch exports to restore the legacy ladder" — but
        # the exports are load-bearing individually: unsetting ONLY
        # FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC (keeping agent-timeout set)
        # must not die on an unbound variable under `set -euo pipefail`;
        # the ceiling defaults to base x4 (exactly what the legacy
        # ladder would have used) before the clip runs.
        run_block = self._shard_run_block()
        self.assertIn(
            '${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}',
            run_block,
        )

    def test_agent_timeout_input_clips_the_watch_ceiling(self):
        # gh-1556 rework review: under the watch the abs ceiling is the
        # cap that actually kills a progressing trial, so an explicit
        # agent-timeout input must clip it to base x4 (pre-PR the legacy
        # ladder did exactly this) — otherwise the tighter cap the
        # operator asked for is silently ignored in favor of the flat
        # 3600s step-env default.
        self.assertIn(
            "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4",
            self._shard_run_block(),
        )

    def test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed(self):
        # gh-1556 rework re-review (suggestion): the escape hatch is
        # "remove the watch exports to restore the legacy ladder" — but
        # the exports are load-bearing individually: unsetting ONLY
        # FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC (keeping agent-timeout set)
        # must not die on an unbound variable under `set -euo pipefail`;
        # the ceiling defaults to base x4 (exactly what the legacy
        # ladder would have used) before the clip runs.

    cross jobs via `needs.setup.outputs.dataset` (the `steps.family`
    ref is only valid inside the setup job itself)."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.text = _HARBOR_YML.read_text()

    @staticmethod
    def _slice_job(text: str, start_marker: str, end_marker: str) -> str:
        # Slice a job body between two literal markers. Assert the markers
        # exist FIRST so a workflow re-indent or a stray `summary:` string
        # fails with a message naming the YAML-shape assumption, not an
        # opaque IndexError from a bare str.split.

            )
        end = text.find(end_marker, start + len(start_marker))
        if end == -1:
            raise AssertionError(
                f"bench-harbor.yml shape changed: end marker {end_marker!r}"
                f" not found after {start_marker!r}"
            )
        return text[start:end]

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux; same pin on `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (audit).
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, clone-around — all produce a valid checkout. Related guard suites: 79 Dart tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the routing label is `macos-m5` (the pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005).
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class, out of scope; AC3 needs that leg resolved too. `bench/mls_bench` has one PRE-EXISTING python REG failure on pristine main (stale `@4.0.0` dataset pin, #1316 drift) — unrelated to this change.

### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).

### Fix

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux; same pin on `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (audit).

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: same pin on `build-macos` (audit); its checkout rides the new action.
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new composite action, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script functionally smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, and clone-around branches all produce a valid checkout.
- Related guard suites (workflow fetch shape, dispatch watch, selfhosted SDK): 79 tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `runs-on: fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the registration label that routes to it is `macos-m5` (the existing pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005) — pinned that way.
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class and out of scope; AC3 (next daily green) needs that leg resolved too.
- bench-mls.yml also runs `self-hosted` but only orchestrates remote sandboxes (no local containers → nothing unremovable); plain leftovers are handled by the tolerant clean.

        gap = float(self._step_env("FA_STALL_GAP_SEC"))

    def _shard_run_block(self):
        """The harbor shard step's `run: |` body."""
        run_block = self.text.split("Run harbor (fa agent", 1)[1]
        return run_block.split("run: |", 1)[1].split("Upload harbor job", 1)[0]

    def test_agent_timeout_input_clips_the_watch_ceiling(self):
        # gh-1556 rework review: under the watch the abs ceiling is the
        # cap that actually kills a progressing trial, so an explicit
        # agent-timeout input must clip it to base x4 (pre-PR the legacy
        # ladder did exactly this) — otherwise the tighter cap the
        # operator asked for is silently ignored in favor of the flat
        # 3600s step-env default.
        self.assertIn(
            "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4",
            self._shard_run_block(),
        )

    def test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed(self):
        # gh-1556 rework re-review (suggestion): the escape hatch is
        # "remove the watch exports to restore the legacy ladder" — but
        # the exports are load-bearing individually: unsetting ONLY
        # FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC (keeping agent-timeout set)
        # must not die on an unbound variable under `set -euo pipefail`;
        # the ceiling defaults to base x4 (exactly what the legacy
        # ladder would have used) before the clip runs.
        run_block = self._shard_run_block()
        self.assertIn(
            '${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}',
            run_block,
        )

class ShardDatasetEnvRegTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """REG (run 38126875911): the bench shard job's harbor step overrode
    DATASET with `${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}` — a `steps.*` ref
    to a step in ANOTHER job always evaluates empty, so every shard died
    with harbor's `Dataset  not found` (empty name). The dataset id must
    cross jobs via `needs.setup.outputs.dataset` (the `steps.family`
    ref is only valid inside the setup job itself)."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.text = _HARBOR_YML.read_text()

    @staticmethod
    def _slice_job(text: str, start_marker: str, end_marker: str) -> str:
        # Slice a job body between two literal markers. Assert the markers
        # exist FIRST so a workflow re-indent or a stray `summary:` string
        # fails with a message naming the YAML-shape assumption, not an
        # opaque IndexError from a bare str.split.
        start = text.find(start_marker)
        if start == -1:
            raise AssertionError(
                f"bench-harbor.yml shape changed: marker {start_marker!r} not found"
            )
        end = text.find(end_marker, start + len(start_marker))
        if end == -1:
            raise AssertionError(
                f"bench-harbor.yml shape changed: end marker {end_marker!r}"
                f" not found after {start_marker!r}"
            )
        return text[start:end]

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe; the kimi coding plan tolerates more — owner picks at dispatch)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # gh-1503: byte-consistent copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 resolve step
      # (same run block, same outputs) — the single-source extraction was
      # rejected there to keep the workflow self-contained; the
      # cross-reference comment in both files is the sync contract. Maps

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux; same pin on `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (audit).

- `bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). - **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: same pin on `build-macos` (audit); its checkout rides the new action.
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new composite action, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, and a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script functionally smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, and clone-around branches all produce a valid checkout.
- Related guard suites (workflow fetch shape, dispatch watch, selfhosted SDK): 79 tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `runs-on: fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the registration label that routes to it is `macos-m5` (the existing pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005) — pinned that way.
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class and out of scope; AC3 (next daily green) needs that leg resolved too.
- bench-mls.yml also runs `self-hosted` but only orchestrates remote sandboxes (no local containers → nothing unremovable); plain leftovers are handled by the tolerant clean.

    def test_agent_timeout_input_clips_the_watch_ceiling(self):
        # gh-1556 rework review: under the watch the abs ceiling is the
        # cap that actually kills a progressing trial, so an explicit
        # agent-timeout input must clip it to base x4 (pre-PR the legacy
        # ladder did exactly this) — otherwise the tighter cap the
        # operator asked for is silently ignored in favor of the flat
        # 3600s step-env default.
        self.assertIn(
            "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4",
            self._shard_run_block(),
        )

    def test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed(self):
        # gh-1556 rework re-review (suggestion): the escape hatch is
        # "remove the watch exports to restore the legacy ladder" — but
        # the exports are load-bearing individually: unsetting ONLY
        # FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC (keeping agent-timeout set)
        # must not die on an unbound variable under `set -euo pipefail`;
        # the ceiling defaults to base x4 (exactly what the legacy
        # ladder would have used) before the clip runs.
        run_block = self._shard_run_block()
        self.assertIn(

    @staticmethod
    def _slice_job(text: str, start_marker: str, end_marker: str) -> str:
        # Slice a job body between two literal markers. Assert the markers
        # exist FIRST so a workflow re-indent or a stray `summary:` string
        # fails with a message naming the YAML-shape assumption, not an

        if end == -1:
            raise AssertionError(
                f"bench-harbor.yml shape changed: end marker {end_marker!r}"
                f" not found after {start_marker!r}"

        return text[start:end]

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).

### Fix

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux; same pin on `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (audit).

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts).     def test_stall_gap_never_drops_below_the_watchdog_invariant(self):
        # gh-1430 invariant: the bench stall-gap must stay above fa's
        # stream-idle watchdog (300s) + margin — the workflow value can
        # never drift below the shipped default (the Dart-source REG in
        # test_fa_agent_timeout.py pins the other side).
        sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
        try:
            import fa_agent_timeout
        finally:
            sys.path.remove(str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
        gap = float(self._step_env("FA_STALL_GAP_SEC"))
        self.assertGreaterEqual(gap, fa_agent_timeout._STALL_GAP_DEFAULT)

    def _shard_run_block(self):
        """The harbor shard step's `run: |` body."""
        run_block = self.text.split("Run harbor (fa agent", 1)[1]
        return run_block.split("run: |", 1)[1].split("Upload harbor job", 1)[0]

    def test_agent_timeout_input_clips_the_watch_ceiling(self):
        # gh-1556 rework review: under the watch the abs ceiling is the
        # cap that actually kills a progressing trial, so an explicit
        # agent-timeout input must clip it to base x4 (pre-PR the legacy
        # ladder did exactly this) — otherwise the tighter cap the
        # operator asked for is silently ignored in favor of the flat
        # 3600s step-env default.
        self.assertIn(
            "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4",
            self._shard_run_block(),
        )

    def test_agent_timeout_clip_defaults_the_ceiling_when_export_removed(self):
        # gh-1556 rework re-review (suggestion): the escape hatch is
        # "remove the watch exports to restore the legacy ladder" — but
        # the exports are load-bearing individually: unsetting ONLY
        # FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC (keeping agent-timeout set)
        # must not die on an unbound variable under `set -euo pipefail`;
        # the ceiling defaults to base x4 (exactly what the legacy
        # ladder would have used) before the clip runs.
        run_block = self._shard_run_block()
        self.assertIn(
            '${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}',
            run_block,
        )

        # gh-1556 rework review: the step env exports FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
        # (the watch default, AC2) — an explicit progress-extension: false
        # dispatch must still win by unsetting it, otherwise the input is
        # a silent no-op while the comment claims otherwise.

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved

# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on

# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.

# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is

# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require

# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation

on:

    inputs:

        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'

# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe; the kimi coding plan tolerates more — owner picks at dispatch)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # gh-1503: byte-consistent copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 resolve step
      # (same run block, same outputs) — the single-source extraction was
      # rejected there to keep the workflow self-contained; the
      # cross-reference comment in both files is the sync contract. Maps

      # model/key env) and preflights the selected secret BEFORE the
      # bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
      # must cost one setup minute, not shard-hours of 429s. Presence

### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

{"content":"### Root Cause

The testflight leg failed on two independent layers (gh-1600):

- **Routing**: `Build iOS IPA` / `Submit iOS to TestFlight` pinned the generic `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` label list, which also matches the Linux self-hosted box — the iOS jobs ran on Linux with no ruby/fastlane/Xcode (`bundle: command not found`, exit 127).
- **Workspace isolation**: bench-harbor wrote its job output INTO the shared self-hosted workspace (`-o jobs` → `jobs/fa-2.1-docker-cpu-14/`, trial dirs bind-mounted into task containers), so the mobile legs' bare `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` hit unremovable leftovers and failed the checkout.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml`: `build-ios` + `submit-ios` pin `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the unique label of the repo's ONE macOS runner (fa-m5-1), never routable onto Linux; same pin on `build-macos.yml` `build-macos` (audit).
- `.github/actions/mirror-checkout` (new, pattern of `setup-flutter-selfhosted`): mirror checkout with a log-and-prune clean — removable leftovers go, a still-blocked remainder moves into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, a surviving stub is cloned around instead of failing the checkout.
- `bench-harbor.yml`: harbor output moved outside the workspace (`-o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"`, uploads follow); new `if: always()` step tears the shard's docker containers down before removing the output dir.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart` — new workflow-lint REG (AC1: every self-hosted job in the mobile/macOS legs carries `macos-m5`, never the generic labels; AC2: bench output outside the workspace + docker teardown before rm + hardened mirror-checkouts). Failed before the fix (9 failures), passes after.
- Action script smoke-tested against a fixture mirror: clean clone, removable leftovers, EBUSY-stub move-aside, clone-around — all produce a valid checkout. Related guard suites: 79 Dart tests passed.

### Notes

- The ticket's `fa-m5-1` is the runner NAME; the routing label is `macos-m5` (the pin `ci.yml` cube-kernel-live has used since gh-1005).
- L2 (fa-extension.zip size budget) is #1262's class, out of scope; AC3 needs that leg resolved too. `bench/mls_bench` has one PRE-EXISTING python REG failure on pristine main (stale `@4.0.0` dataset pin, #1316 drift) — unrelated to this change.
